chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is the dowry, meaning in mut'ah (temporary marriage)?' He said, 'Whatever they agree upon until whatever duration they choose.'
And whenever the woman differs from the man or delays from him from the total of the days stipulated for her, then he has the right to withhold from her dowry in proportion to that.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dowry and duration in Shia temporary marriage (mut'ah)?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the dowry in *mut'ah* is not fixed by a statutory limit but is entirely contingent upon the mutual consent (*taradi*) of both parties for the specified duration. It further establishes the principle of proportional deduction, allowing the husband to withhold a portion of the dowry corresponding to any days the wife fails to fulfill her obligation of availability, a key distinction from permanent marriage in Shia jurisprudence.
